Autonomous Decision-Making under Environment & System Uncertainties

A.

Safety vs. Multimodality in Generative AI Planning

Broad Problem

In robot planning problems, generative AI methods (diffusion models, flow-matching, etc.) can represent multimodal behaviors (e.g., a robot arm picking up a cup in multiple different positions). However, this flexibility conflicts inherently with safety, stability, and related guarantees crucial to closed-loop control.

로봇 planning 문제에서 generative AI 기법(diffusion model, flow-matching 등)은 multimodal한 행동을 표현할 수 있습니다(예: 로봇 팔이 컵을 여러 다른 위치에서 집는 경우). 그러나 이러한 유연성은 closed-loop control에서 핵심적인 safety, stability 및 관련 보장과 본질적으로 충돌합니다.

Research Goal

Develop generative AI-based planning algorithms for autonomous (robotic) agents that fundamentally encode safety/stability constraints without losing multimodal flexibility. Current methods of investigation include designing hierarchical safety filters and distributional control formulations.

자율(로봇) 에이전트를 위한 generative AI 기반 planning 알고리즘을 개발합니다. multimodal한 유연성을 잃지 않으면서 safety/stability 제약을 근본적으로 내재화하는 알고리즘입니다. 현재 검토 중인 방법에는 hierarchical safety filter 설계와 distributional control 정식화가 있습니다.

Application Areas
Generative AI for roboticsDiffusion/Flow-matchingSafe/Robust autonomyTrajectory and motion planning
B.

Robust & Adaptive Control with Uncertainty Quantification

Broad Problem

Real-world autonomous systems often experience external environment uncertainties and unmodeled dynamics. In particular, when stochastic effects are nonstationary (e.g., highly-dynamic environments, interaction-awareness), many stochastic control algorithms can experience poor adaptability and robustness.

실제 환경의 자율 시스템은 외부 환경의 불확실성과 모델링되지 않은 dynamics를 자주 겪습니다. 특히 stochastic한 영향이 nonstationary할 때(예: 변화가 큰 환경, interaction-awareness가 필요한 상황) 많은 stochastic control 알고리즘은 적응성과 robustness가 크게 떨어집니다.

Research Goal

Develop path-planners that are robust and adaptive especially against nonstationary uncertainties, by combining both model-based and data-driven methods. Current methods of investigation include classical set prediction & propagation methods, learning-based OOD detectors (e.g., random network distillation), and online reinforcement learning.

model-based 방법과 data-driven 방법을 결합해 특히 nonstationary한 불확실성에 robust하고 adaptive한 path-planner를 개발합니다. 현재 검토 중인 방법으로는 고전적인 set prediction & propagation, learning-based OOD detector(예: random network distillation), online reinforcement learning이 있습니다.

Application Areas
Fault-tolerant systemsOOD detection for controlAutonomous trajectory and motion planningOnline reinforcement learning

Large-Scale Control and Estimation for Networks / Multiagent Systems

A.

Robust & Adaptive Large-Scale Network Control

Broad Problem

Scalable implementations of stochastic control and state-estimation algorithms introduce additional uncertainties (e.g., dynamic graph topology, delayed information transmission among agents) and constraints (e.g., limited communication bandwidth, lack of coordination among agents).

stochastic control과 state-estimation 알고리즘을 확장 가능하게 구현하면 추가적인 불확실성(예: 동적으로 변하는 graph topology, 에이전트 간 정보 전달 지연)과 제약(예: 제한된 통신 대역폭, 에이전트 간 coordination 부재)이 생깁니다.

Research Goal

Develop distributed/decentralized stochastic control and state-estimation algorithms for large-scale systems that are robust, adaptive, and scalable (i.e., localizable) to high-dimensional network uncertainties. Current methods of investigation include system level synthesis, consensus methods, and others.

large-scale 시스템에 쓸 distributed/decentralized stochastic control 및 state-estimation 알고리즘을 개발합니다. 고차원 network 불확실성에 robust하고 adaptive하며 scalable(즉, localizable)한 알고리즘을 목표로 합니다. 지금은 system level synthesis, consensus 기법 등을 검토하고 있습니다.

Application Areas
Multi-agent systemsLarge-scale networksFault-tolerant controlConsensusSystem level synthesis
B.

Situational Awareness with Wireless Sensor Networks

Broad Problem

Real-time situational awareness for large-scale environments requires a delicate balance between efficiency and accuracy. However, many conventional data-gathering architectures have the external sensors transmit all their measurements to the decision-making central agent, increasing traffic congestion and unnecessarily redundant communications. In the case of visual data, high computation and power demands for processing can cause large reconstruction errors from asynchronous sensor updates.

대규모 환경의 실시간 situational awareness에서는 효율성과 정확도 사이에서 정교하게 균형을 맞춰야 합니다. 하지만 기존의 많은 data-gathering 구조에서는 외부 sensor가 모든 측정값을 의사결정 중심 에이전트로 전송합니다. 이 때문에 트래픽 혼잡과 불필요하게 중복된 통신이 늘어납니다. 시각 데이터의 경우 처리에 필요한 연산량과 전력 요구가 높아 asynchronous한 sensor 갱신으로 인한 reconstruction 오차가 커질 수 있습니다.

Research Goal

Develop architectures for large-scale, distributed estimation and scene reconstruction, with special focus on improving data preprocessing and transmission to optimally balance network efficiency and good reconstruction performance. Current methods of investigation include sensor scheduling, and 3D Gaussian splats.

large-scale distributed estimation과 scene reconstruction을 위한 구조를 개발합니다. 데이터 전처리와 전송을 개선해 network 효율성과 좋은 reconstruction 성능이 최적으로 균형을 이루도록 하는 데 집중합니다. 현재 검토 중인 방법으로는 sensor scheduling과 3D Gaussian splat이 있습니다.

Application Areas
Distributed data-gatheringMulti-target TrackingDistributed 3D reconstructionSensor networksRobotic sensor networks

Data-Efficient Online Learning for Adaptive Autonomous Systems

A.

Control-Relevant Latent Representations for Embodied AI

Broad Problem

AGI architectures (e.g., VLAMs) offer a powerful foundation for complex autonomous decision-making and embodied AI. However, their internal representations are often difficult to analyze, especially when 1) conditions like visual inputs, language inputs, or contexts change, and when 2) when tasks must be performed sequentially over time without catastrophic forgetting.

AGI 구조(예: VLAM)는 복잡한 자율 의사결정과 embodied AI의 강력한 토대가 됩니다. 그러나 내부 표현은 분석이 어려운 경우가 많습니다. 특히 1) 시각 입력, 언어 입력, context 같은 조건이 바뀔 때, 그리고 2) catastrophic forgetting 없이 여러 task를 시간에 걸쳐 순차적으로 수행해야 할 때 그렇습니다.

Research Goal

Develop control-relevant latent representations and geometric models of the latent space for VLAM-based decision makers. Develop, in particular, a “similarity metric” on the latent space so that semantically-equivalent observations remain close. Current methods of investigation include manifold steering, dimensionality reduction, and group equivariance.

VLAM 기반 의사결정기를 위한 control-relevant latent representation과 latent space의 기하학적 모델을 개발합니다. 특히 의미적으로 동등한 관측이 서로 가깝게 유지되도록 latent space 상의 “similarity metric”을 만듭니다. 현재 검토 중인 방법으로는 manifold steering, 차원 축소, group equivariance가 있습니다.

Application Areas
Vision-language-action modelsWorld modelsEmbodied AIHuman-robot interactionContinuous ControlRepresentation learning
B.

Data-Efficient Adaptation and Active Learning

Broad Problem

Real-world data collection for robotic control is often expensive, sparse, and safety-critical. This means naive methods of fine-tuning and training are often unsuitable for robotic systems, especially if they must learn to adapt to new tasks and environments.

로봇 제어용 실제 데이터 수집은 비용이 크고 희소하며 safety-critical한 경우가 많습니다. 따라서 단순한 fine-tuning이나 학습 방식은 로봇 시스템에 적합하지 않은 경우가 많습니다. 새로운 task와 환경에 적응해야 할 때는 더욱 그렇습니다.

Research Goal

Develop methods for improving robot performance by identifying the most valuable data samples and allowing agents to make decisions quickly (with accelerated convergence towards the optimal hyperparameters). Current methods of investigation include adaptive gradient descent, active learning, and stochastic optimization.

로봇 성능을 개선하는 방법을 개발합니다. 이 방법은 가장 가치 있는 데이터 샘플을 식별하고 에이전트가 빠르게 결정을 내리도록(최적 hyperparameter로 수렴하는 속도를 높여) 합니다. adaptive gradient descent, active learning, stochastic optimization을 현재 검토하고 있습니다.

Application Areas
Optimization methods in MLActive learningOnline learningStochastic ApproximationData-efficient control
